title: Logged-model store tests go in test_sqlalchemy_store_runs.py and must cover repeated keys
answers: where should logged model tag store tests be added
test placement for logged model store methods in sqlalchemy_store
do sqlalchemy store tests run against Postgres and MySQL in CI
add a test for duplicate tag keys in logged models
body:
Convention: Store tests for logged models (create, get, tags) live in tests/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store/test_sqlalchemy_store_runs.py, next to the existing logged-model tests, not in test_sqlalchemy_store_core.py.
The sqlalchemy_store test suite is run in CI against SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MSSQL, so a dialect-specific upsert bug only shows up there.
For tag upserts, the test must include a repeated-key case in one call (expects the last value), because that is the case that fails on PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT.
The test test_set_logged_model_tags_bulk_upsert covers clean insert, overwrite, empty list, a batch above the batch_size=100 boundary, and a repeated key.
Do not leave trailing blank lines at end of file; ruff format flags them.
applies: New or changed tests for SqlAlchemyStore logged model methods and their tag upserts.
says: Saving tags on a logged model fails when the same tag name is repeated.
Updating metadata tags crashes when providing duplicate keys in a single bulk request.
Tagging a logged model with duplicate keys triggers database errors on Postgres backends.
Ensure batch tag updates apply the latest value when duplicate tag keys are submitted.
search: Logged model store tests for `SqlAlchemyStore` belong in `tests/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store/test_sqlalchemy_store_runs.py` rather than `test_sqlalchemy_store_core.py`. Tag upsert tests (`SqlAlchemyStore.set_logged_model_tags`) must include a duplicate-key case expecting the last value to catch dialect-specific PostgreSQL `ON CONFLICT` errors during CI runs across SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MSSQL. `test_set_logged_model_tags_bulk_upsert` covers insert, overwrite, empty lists, batches over 100 items, and repeated keys without trailing blank lines.
